page.title: Settings
page.subtitle: Connect any system: push leads out, receive or pull them in, and let other systems use your API.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.keyNameHint: Header or query parameter name, e.g. X-Api-Key, API-Key, api_key
auth.tokenUrlHint: Leadrat fetches and refreshes the access token automatically
auth.signatureHeaderInbound: Header the sender puts the signature in
auth.signatureHeaderOutbound: Header Leadrat puts the signature in

errors.unclosedSingle: Unclosed single quote in cURL command
errors.unclosedDouble: Unclosed double quote in cURL command
errors.notCurl: Paste a command that starts with "curl"
errors.noUrl: No URL found in the cURL command

mapping.notObject: Field mapping is available when the body template is a JSON object. Edit the template directly below.
mapping.title: Field Mapping - {{mapped}} of {{count}} client keys mapped to CRM fields

delivery.title: Delivery Detail - {{id}}
delivery.passExplainer: A "Pass" here only means the target server returned an HTTP 2xx status - it does not confirm the receiving system actually stored or processed the lead. Check the response body above for what it actually said; if it's blank or just an acknowledgement, that system may be receiving the request but rejecting or ignoring the payload internally (wrong field names/format for its API, a required field on its side that this payload doesn't include, etc).

push.title: Outbound Webhooks - Push Leads & Updates
push.intro: Fully customisable per webhook: JSON, Form (x-www-form-urlencoded), or your own Custom body template with <fieldkey></fieldkey> placeholders (e.g. <example></example>) - works like filling in a cURL command once.
push.curlHelp: Paste the example request their API docs or Postman gives you (with real or sample data). The URL, method and headers are copied as-is, and every key in the body is listed below so you can choose which CRM field fills it for each lead.
push.curlPrompt: Have the client's cURL? <action>Import from cURL</action> to fill this in and map fields automatically.
push.urlVariables: The URL can contain variables too, e.g. <urlexample></urlexample>.
push.headersInvalid: Headers must be valid JSON, e.g. {{example}}
push.authTitle: Authentication (how Leadrat signs in to their API)
push.modeSame: Send every event to the same URL
push.modeCreateUpdate: Create the record once, then update that same record (no duplicates on their side)
push.responseIdRequired: Their record ID in the response *
push.responseIdOptional: Their record ID in the response (optional)
push.responseIdHint: Where the ID is in their JSON reply to the create request. Saved per lead as <externalid></externalid>.
push.retriesHint: For timeouts, HTTP 429 and 5xx errors - after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h.
push.howFilled: How values get filled in: this webhook is reused for every lead - Leadrat doesn't send a static example, it sends a fresh push each time a selected event happens, with THAT lead's current values.
push.howFilledStandard: JSON / Form automatically include every field on the lead - nothing to set up.
push.howFilledCustom: Custom - write your own request body and drop in anywhere; each one is swapped for that lead's real value right before sending. Click a variable below to insert it.
push.rawTemplate: Body Template (raw) - edit directly or insert variables
push.preview: Preview - what will actually be sent (sample lead)
push.previewEmpty: (write a body template above to see a preview)
push.deleteConfirm: Delete webhook "{{name}}"? This cannot be undone.
push.resyncTruncated_one: Resync pushed the first {{total}} of {{count}} lead (limit {{limit}} per run). Narrow the date range to push the rest.
push.resyncTruncated_other: Resync pushed the first {{total}} of {{count}} leads (limit {{limit}} per run). Narrow the date range to push the rest.
push.syncHelp: Push every lead registered in this date range again (leave both blank to push everything).

deliveries.title: Delivery Log
deliveries.help: Every push attempt - pass, fail, and why - so a failed delivery is never silent.

sources.saveFirst: Save the source first, then test it.
sources.sampleInvalid: The example payload must be valid JSON
sources.deleteConfirm: Delete "{{name}}"? Leads already imported stay; the link to their records is removed.
sources.step1: 1. Get a sample of their data
sources.sampleFound_one: {{count}} record found in the sample, {{fields}} to choose from.
sources.sampleFound_other: {{count}} records found in the sample, {{fields}} to choose from.
sources.recordsPath: Where the list of records is
sources.recordsPathPlaceholder: blank = the whole body is one record (or a list)
sources.externalIdPath: Their record ID (to update instead of duplicate)
sources.defaultCountry: Country for numbers without a code
sources.updateExisting: Update the lead when the same record comes again
sources.showAll_one: Show all {{count}} field to map more
sources.showAll_other: Show all {{count}} fields to map more
sources.statusMapHelp: If you mapped Status, translate their status values to yours. Unlisted values are used as-is.
sources.previewStale: The mapping changed since this preview - <action>refresh the preview</action>.

receive.title: Receive - Accept Leads in Any Format
receive.intro: Each source gets its own URL. Point Facebook lead ads, Zapier, a website form or another CRM's webhook at it - they send leads in their own JSON or form format, and you map their fields to yours.
receive.urlIntro: Your receive URL - give this to the sending system (POST, JSON or form-encoded):
receive.newUrlConfirm: Generate a new URL? The old one stops working immediately.
receive.sendExample: Send one example first - it is captured as a sample (nothing is imported until the mapping below is saved).
receive.securityAuthTitle: Only accept requests signed with this secret
receive.sampleLabel: Example payload (paste one, or leave blank to use the last request received)

pull.title: Pull - Fetch Leads from Any API
pull.intro: Leadrat calls another system's API on a schedule (any auth, any paging) and imports the records it returns. Records it has seen before update the same lead.
pull.variables: Variables: <since></since> (last successful run, ISO time; empty the first time), <others></others>
pull.sampleHelp: Save, then Fetch sample - Leadrat calls the API once (first page only) and imports nothing.

inbound.title: Received Records
inbound.help: Every record that came in and what happened to it.

api.title: Your API - Two-Way Access for Any System
api.intro: Any system with your API key can create, read and update leads and subscribe to lead events. Send the key in the <hdr></hdr> header, as <bearer></bearer>, or (if the tool can't set headers) as <query></query>. Limit: {{limit}} requests per minute.
api.noPermission: Only someone with the Manage Settings permission can view the API key.
api.shownOnce: Copy this key now and store it somewhere safe - for security it is only shown once. If it's lost, generate a new one.
api.regenerateConfirm: Generate a new API key? The current key stops working immediately for every system using it.
api.openApiHint: Import the OpenAPI spec into Postman, Zapier, Make or n8n to get every endpoint ready to use.

endpoints.createLead: Create a lead (send your own ID as externalReferenceId - repeats never duplicate)
endpoints.listLeads: List leads changed since a time, oldest first - for incremental sync
endpoints.findLead: Find a lead by your own ID
endpoints.fields: Every field a lead can carry, and where it goes in the request
endpoints.subscribe: Subscribe a URL to lead events: {{example}}

api.exampleList: Read leads changed since a time (incremental sync)
api.exampleSubscribe: Get notified of lead events (your system receives a POST with the lead as JSON)
api.examplesFooter: Subscriptions appear on the Push tab, where you can add authentication or a custom body. If the other system sends leads in its own format instead of this one, use the Receive tab.
